name: runbook-rotate-logs
description: Rotate oversized logs on a host: find the large and unrotated log files and whether logrotate covers them, approval, rotation (logrotate -f for configured ones, copy-and-truncate for the rest - never deleting a log a process has open), and verification of the sizes and that the writers still log.

report.title: Find large logs
report.prompt:
Host {{input.host}}, logs under {{input.path}}. Read-only (ssh_exec runs as the host's read-only account by default): the biggest files (du -xsk, find -size +50M), which process has each open (lsof if present), and whether logrotate has a rule for it (cat /etc/logrotate.conf /etc/logrotate.d/*). Plan, per file: logrotate -f <its config> when configured, otherwise cp <file> <file>.<date> && gzip the copy && truncate -s 0 <file> (keeps the open file handle). Nothing changes now.

Report: the files with sizes, the exact rotation command for each, and the space it frees.

rotate.title: Rotate
rotate.prompt:
A person approved this rotation on {{input.host}}:
{{state.report}}

Run exactly those rotation commands with ssh_exec as: "operator", one file at a time, and nothing else.

Report: each command and its result.

verify.title: Verify
verify.prompt:
Verify the log rotation on {{input.host}}: the rotated files are small again, the rotated copies exist (compressed), and each writer still writes to its log (its size grows or its last line is recent; logs_search or tail). host_stats for the disk. VERIFIED or FAILED.

Report: sizes before and after.
